$schema: Aptos design tokens — canonical source for the aptos-design-system skill

sourceOfTruth.brandGuidelines: Figma 'Aptos Brand Guidelines' (Color Overview p.25, Type Usage p.20, Fallbacks: Serif p.21) — screenshots provided by user 2026-08-20
sourceOfTruth.crossCheckedAgainst: https://github.com/aptos-labs/explorer/blob/main/app/themes/colors/aptosBrandColors.ts and typography.ts (official Aptos Explorer, MIT-licensed source, live as of 2026-08-20)
sourceOfTruth.note: Both sources agree exactly on the 11 raw brand hex values. The explorer source additionally supplies tested, WCAG-AA-passing derived colors for text/interactive use, which the raw brand guideline does not define. Treat raw brand colors as fill/surface/dark-mode-text colors; treat the derived a11y colors as light-mode interactive text/status colors.

mint.role: Core brand color. Fills, illustration, iconography, dark-mode success text. Never as light-mode body/link text (fails contrast).

babyBlue.role: Secondary. Fills, illustration, dark-mode info/primary text. Never as light-mode body/link text (fails contrast).

coral.role: Secondary. Fills, illustration, dark-mode error/warning text. Never as light-mode body/link text (fails contrast).

ink.role: Primary text on light surfaces; dark-mode paper/card background.

graphite.role: Secondary text on light surfaces; dark-mode border-light.

tan.role: Decorative / large-scale only. FAILS WCAG AA as text on White or Creme (2.9:1, 2.5:1) — do not use for body text on light backgrounds.

sand.role: Neutral surface tint; passes AAA as text on dark neutrals only.

creme.role: Warm off-white. Dark-mode secondary text; light-mode alt surface.

white.role: Warm off-white. Dark-mode primary text; brand-warm light surface (see canvas note below).

serif.cssStack: "IBM Plex Serif", Georgia, "Times New Roman", Times, serif
serif.use: Display headings, h1–h3. Licensed brand font — self-host under public/fonts/ if you obtain a license; otherwise ship the open fallback.

sans.cssStack: "IBM Plex Sans", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
sans.use: Body copy, navigation, UI text, h4–h6.

mono.cssStack: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace
mono.use: Tertiary/subtitle labels, addresses, hashes, on-chain numeric data, proposal IDs.

typography.knownDivergence: The official Aptos Explorer app's MUI theme.ts implements h1/h2 as serif weight 600 tracking -0.02em (matches guideline), but implements its 'subtitle1' as uppercase SANS with 0.06em tracking rather than the brand guideline's literal 'Tertiary = Akkurat Mono' rule for subtitles. Both are legitimate; pick one and be consistent. This skill's governance token set follows the literal brand guideline (mono for tertiary/subtitle) since it reads better for on-chain IDs and addresses.

light.canvasChoiceNote: Two legitimate light-mode canvas choices exist in real Aptos sources: a warm cream '#F9F9F0' (matches the brand guideline's own White/Creme neutrals, and the aptosnetwork.com marketing site's warm editorial direction) vs. a neutral grey '#ECEEF2' with white cards (the official Explorer app's deliberate 'traditional app chrome' choice, its own code comment says this is INSTEAD of bright-cream-on-bright-warm-white). Pick one per project and document the choice; do not mix them on the same screen.

governanceExtension.note: Not part of the raw brand guideline or the Explorer app — derived for this project by combining verified brand fills with verified a11y-safe text colors. Every pairing below is contrast-checked in scripts/check_contrast.py.
governanceExtension.proposalStatusModelNote: CORRECTED 2026-08-20 after reading the live on-chain framework (aptos_framework::voting, aptos_governance). There is no 'not yet started' or 'expired' proposal state — voting power/eligibility is fixed at creation and voting is open immediately. voting::get_proposal_state() returns only PENDING (voting still open) or SUCCEEDED/FAILED (voting closed); is_resolved is a SEPARATE bool tracking whether the resolution script has actually run. The real lifecycle is: active (voting open) -> passed (voting closed, succeeded, not yet resolved) -> executed (is_resolved == true) as the happy path, or active -> failed (voting closed, did not meet threshold) as the terminal unhappy path. The earlier 'pending' and 'expired' tokens below were replaced with 'passed' because they didn't correspond to any real on-chain state.

active.rationale: voting::is_voting_closed() == false — voting still open. Baby Blue, matches Explorer's info/in-progress mapping.

passed.rationale: get_proposal_state() == SUCCEEDED but is_resolved == false — voting succeeded, awaiting on-chain execution. Mint, matches Explorer's success mapping.

executed.rationale: is_resolved == true — fully resolved/executed on-chain, now historical. Graphite, muted/archived treatment (deliberately distinct from the still-actionable Mint 'passed' state).

failed.rationale: get_proposal_state() == FAILED — voting closed without meeting min_vote_threshold or majority voted no. Coral, matches Explorer's error mapping.

for.rationale: Bar/fill uses raw Mint (safe as a large fill); the numeric vote count next to it uses the a11y-derived success green in light mode so the number itself is readable as text, not just decorative.

against.rationale: Same pattern with Coral / derived error red.
